sermon.title: Understanding Sin
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer explains Bible sin from Cain and Abel: God rejected Cain’s evil works, not merely his produce offering. He distinguishes shadow, spiritual, wise and civil laws, names rejecting Christ as the hell-sending spiritual law, shows sin hurts neighbors more than it “hurts” God, and closes with Joseph’s refusal and Job’s repentance that turns captivity.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Sensitive: homosexuality/same-sex marriage, abortion, slavery-law civil disobedience, Supreme Court, public/government schools as humanist. Allah vs Jesus name. Keep as spoken. Caption “herod” for Potiphar corrected.

chunks.section_question: Why did God reject Cain’s offering if produce was acceptable?
chunks.short_answer: Genesis 4: Cain’s produce offering vs Abel’s flock; God respected Abel and his offering, not Cain. Leviticus 5:7–11 shows flour from the ground can be a sin offering, so rejection was not because fruit of the ground was invalid. Shadow offerings never took away sin (Hebrews 10:4); they pointed to Jesus the Lamb. Isaiah 1: God wants people to stop evil and learn to do good.

‘If he is not able to bring a lamb, then he shall bring to the LORD, for his trespass which he has committed, two turtledoves or two young pigeons: one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. And he shall bring them to the priest, who shall offer that which is for the sin offering first, and wring off its head from its neck, but shall not divide it completely. Then he shall sprinkle some of the blood of the sin offering on the side of the altar, and the rest of the blood shall be drained out at the base of the altar. It is a sin offering. And he shall offer the second as a burnt offering according to the prescribed manner. So the priest shall make atonement on his behalf for his sin which he has committed, and it shall be forgiven him. ‘But if he is not able to bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons, then he who sinned shall bring for his offering one-tenth of an ephah of fine flour as a sin offering. He shall put no oil on it, nor shall he put frankincense on it, for it is a sin offering.
For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and goats could take away sins.

“To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?” Says the LORD. “I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams And the fat of fed cattle. I do not delight in the blood of bulls, Or of lambs or goats. “When you come to appear before Me, Who has required this from your hand, To trample My courts? Bring no more futile sacrifices; Incense is an abomination to Me. The New Moons, the Sabbaths, and the calling of assemblies— I cannot endure iniquity and the sacred meeting. Your New Moons and your appointed feasts My soul hates; They are a trouble to Me, I am weary of bearing them. When you spread out your hands, I will hide My eyes from you; Even though you make many prayers, I will not hear. Your hands are full of blood. “Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; Put away the evil of your doings from before My eyes. Cease to do evil, Learn to do good; Seek justice, Rebuke the oppressor; Defend the fatherless, Plead for the widow.

chunks.section_question: Why was Cain “of the wicked one”?
chunks.short_answer: First John 3:8: he who commits sin is of the Devil; the Devil sinned from the beginning and enticed Eve and Cain. First John 3:11–12: Cain was of the wicked one and slew Abel because his own works were evil and Abel’s righteous—God rejected Cain’s lifestyle, not merely the type of sacrifice.

chunks.section_question: What is sin, and which laws send you to hell?

Spiritual laws (pray, lift hands, tithe) matter, but you do not burn in hell for missing them. One spiritual law sends to hell: rejecting Jesus Christ after hearing and being drawn (John 3). Wise laws avoid evil and save for hard times.

“I have heard of You by the hearing of the ear, But now my eye sees You. Therefore I abhor myself, And repent in dust and ashes.” And so it was, after the LORD had spoken these words to Job, that the LORD said to Eliphaz the Temanite, “My wrath is aroused against you and your two friends, for you have not spoken of Me what is right, as My servant Job has. Now therefore, take for yourselves seven bulls and seven rams, go to My servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and My servant Job shall pray for you. And the LORD restored Job’s losses when he prayed for his friends. Indeed the LORD gave Job twice as much as he had before.

faqs.question: Was fruit of the ground an acceptable sin offering?
faqs.answer: From Leviticus 5, if unable to bring a lamb or birds, fine flour could be a sin offering—so Cain’s rejection was not because produce was invalid.

faqs.question: Can the blood of bulls and goats take away sin?
faqs.answer: Hebrews 10:4 says it is not possible; Abel’s lamb pointed to Jesus, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world.

scriptures.text_nkjv: For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and goats could take away sins.

faqs.question: Why did Cain kill Abel?
faqs.answer: Because his own works were evil and Abel’s were righteous; he wanted acceptance while doing wrong and got mad when God honored the just man.

faqs.question: Do you go to hell for not praying, lifting hands, or tithing?
faqs.answer: He says those are spiritual laws you violate if you don’t do them, but there is no Scripture that you burn in hell for that—except rejecting Jesus Christ.

faqs.question: What is the one spiritual law that sends you to hell?
faqs.answer: Rejecting the Lord Jesus Christ after he has been preached and the Holy Ghost has convicted and drawn you.

faqs.question: Is God a respecter of persons regarding who must live right?
faqs.answer: Acts 10:34: God is no respecter of persons; people in other nations who do right without hearing of Christ can still go to heaven.

faqs.question: How do we know a law is bad?
faqs.answer: Because it harms other innocent people—bad laws mistreat people while the world around you goes to hell.

faqs.question: Does your sin accomplish something against God?
faqs.answer: From Job 35, you don’t dismantle God; your wickedness affects a man such as you—neighbors and family.

scriptures.text_nkjv: If you sin, what do you accomplish against Him? Or, if your transgressions are multiplied, what do you do to Him? If you are righteous, what do you give Him? Or what does He receive from your hand? Your wickedness affects a man such as you, And your righteousness a son of man.

faqs.question: Who intercedes when we sin against our neighbor?
faqs.answer: Jesus Christ intercedes (Hebrews / 1 John); if you sin against God, that question presses who will intercede.

faqs.question: What turned Job’s captivity?
faqs.answer: When Job repented in dust and ashes and prayed for his friends, the Lord accepted him and turned his captivity—gospel pattern of forgiveness and freedom from bondage.
